correctness.rationale: A spanning tree deletes exactly two edges, from distinct paths or the other two paths would form a cycle. Conversely cutting one edge on each of two paths connects both resulting pieces of each via the intact path. In weighted tree edge-voltage coordinates the tree energy is Euclidean, and the two omitted-edge energies are squared signed sums along their replacement paths. Their two coefficient vectors have Gram matrix diag(ℓ_i−1,ℓ_j−1)+(ℓ_r/w_r)vvᵀ with v=(√w_i,±√w_j), since the only shared edges are in arm r. This verifies positive definiteness, both nonunit eigenvalues, the n−3 unit eigenvalues on the quotient, and position independence. The diagonal entries are exactly the two omitted stretches. For (2,2,3) and (6,6,t), the two short-retention objectives increase while the two long-retention objectives decrease. Direct substitution gives equality at 36/5 for the upper eigenvalue increments and at 3(√57−3)/2 for stretch, with 7 strictly in between, so the optimizer sets are disjoint exactly on the claimed interval. At t=7, exact grounded Laplacian determinants independently gave monic polynomials (λ−1)^3(3λ²−28λ+50)/3 and (λ−1)^3(λ−2)(7λ−50)/7 for short and long retention. At n=5 all arms have length two and both objectives increase with (sum of other weights)/w_r, so they share the same maximizing-weight retained arms even at ties.
